pools._comment: Scrap roll. A fridge is mostly sheet steel and moulded plastic, with the control board's electronics rarer.

_comment: Secondary roll: what was left in the freezer. The only ice or snow in this world - the
garbage biome has no weather that makes either.
PACKED ice, not minecraft:ice, and the distinction is the water economy. Plain ice broken
without silk touch on solid ground leaves a water SOURCE block, and two sources are
infinite water - so it would retire the Rain Collector, the bucket gate and the
farmland-hydration half of encroachment immunity (#156) in one drop. leachate_is_not_water
already states that rule for fluids; an item walks through the same door.
Packed ice never melts and yields no water, so the freezer still contains something icy.
Component roll, and the knowledge follows it. A fridge holds a compressor motor, a
refrigerant pump and an interior bulb, so which one you recover is a lottery - and whichever
comes out is the one you learn.
NO FILLER ENTRY, deliberately. You always get exactly one component; what you never get is to
choose which. That is what keeps a_component_teardown_always_yields_a_component true after the
owner's 2026-08-12 ruling that the lottery overrides the old one-object-one-component rule.
